domain: California license renewal and home improvement business rules (CSLB): contractor license expiration, renewal, delinquency, retroactive renewal and refusal for unpaid tax/agency liabilities; Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration, renewal and employer notices; prohibited inducements and fraud; home improvement contract (B&P 7159) mandatory contents, headings, typeface, notices, downpayment and progress-payment limits, right-to-cancel (3/5/7-day) notices; security interests and lender payment methods; service and repair contracts (<= $750); loan-contingent contracts; single-family dwelling construction contracts; swimming pool financing, void pool contracts and attorney fees; solar energy system disclosure document
source_doc: 2026 CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book (official), Section VI, B&P Code end of Article 8 (Construction Management Education Account grants 7139.4-7139.10, skipped as board administration), Article 9 'Renewal of Licenses' (7140-7145.5) and Article 10 'Home Improvement Business' (7150-7169), PDF pages 380-431; file chunk lawbook_p381-430.txt. Note: the chunk label mentioned disciplinary/workers comp/revenue sections, but the actual text in this chunk is the CM education grant program, license renewal and home improvement business.

rules.title: Contractor license expires two years from last day of month issued
rules.plain_english: A California contractor license expires two years after the last day of the month in which it was issued. After each renewal, it expires two years after the date it last expired.

parameters.anchor_original_license: last day of the month in which the license is issued
parameters.anchor_renewed_license: date on which the renewed license last expired
parameters.formula: first_expiration = last_day_of_month(issue_date) + 2 years; next_expiration = previous_expiration + 2 years

rules.applies_to: All contractor licenses issued by CSLB
rules.verbatim_quote: All licenses issued under the provisions of this chapter shall expire two years from the last day of the month in which the license is issued, or two years from the date on which the renewed license last expired.
rules.notes: Renewal fee and delinquency fee amounts are set in the fee section of the chapter (B&P 7137), which is not in this excerpt.

verification.note: Both anchors (last day of month issued; date renewed license last expired) and the 2-year term match.

rules.title: Renew before expiration to keep license continuous
rules.plain_english: To renew a license that has not expired, file the CSLB renewal form and pay the renewal fee before the expiration date. A timely renewal keeps the license active for the next two years.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with an unexpired license
rules.verbatim_quote: To renew a license which has not expired, the licensee shall, before the time at which the license would otherwise expire, apply for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and pay the renewal fee prescribed by this chapter.
rules.notes: A software reminder should trigger well before the expiration date because an incomplete application can be rejected (see B&P 7141(b), 7145).

rules.title: Expired license may be renewed within 5 years; unlicensed during the gap
rules.plain_english: An expired license can be renewed any time within five years after it expired by filing a renewal application and paying the renewal fee plus the delinquency fee. The renewal takes effect only on the date an acceptable application is filed, so the contractor is unlicensed between the expiration date and that date.

parameters.renewal_effective_on: date an acceptable renewal application is filed with the board

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors whose license has expired
rules.verbatim_quote: Renewal under this section shall be effective on the date an acceptable renewal application is filed with the board. The licensee shall be considered unlicensed and there will be a break in the licensing time between the expiration date and the date the renewal becomes effective.
rules.notes: Retroactive renewal under B&P 7141.5 (within 90 days) can avoid the gap. Contracting during a gap is unlicensed work (consequences are covered in other sections of the book).

verification.note: 5-year window, effective-on-filing rule, licensing gap and delinquency fee (except as provided in (b)) match. SB 822 effective 1/1/2014 confirmed in history note.

rules.title: 30-day grace on delinquency fee for returned incomplete renewal
rules.plain_english: If a renewal filed on or before the expiration date is returned as incomplete, you have 30 days after the expiration date to send back a corrected application without paying the delinquency fee. The license still shows as expired until the correct application is submitted.

parameters.condition: original renewal application submitted on or before expiration date and returned as incomplete

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose timely renewal application was rejected as incomplete
rules.verbatim_quote: If a corrected and acceptable renewal application is not returned within 30 days after the license expiration date, the delinquency fee shall apply. The 30 day grace period shall apply only to the delinquency fee.
rules.notes: The grace period does not prevent the expired status: the license shows expired for any period between the expiration date and submission of a correct application.

verification.note: 30 days after the expiration date, delinquency-fee-only grace and expired status until a correct application is submitted all match. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2014).

rules.title: Late renewal runs only to the next regular expiration date
rules.plain_english: A license renewed after it expired does not get a fresh two-year term from the renewal date. It stays in effect only until the next regular two-year expiration date under B&P 7140.

parameters.renewed_license_expires_on: next B&P 7140 expiration date occurring after the effective date of the renewal

rules.verbatim_quote: If so renewed, the license shall continue in effect through the date provided in Section 7140 that next occurs after the effective date of the renewal, when it shall expire if it is not again renewed.

verification.note: Renewal runs to the next 7140 date after the renewal takes effect. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2014).

rules.title: License not renewed within 5 years: apply for a new license
rules.plain_english: If a license is not renewed within five years after it expired, it can no longer be renewed. The person must apply for a new license, pay all original-license fees and meet all qualifications and requirements for an original license.

requirements: pay all fees for an original license
meet all qualifications and requirements for an original license

rules.applies_to: Former licensees whose license expired more than 5 years ago
rules.verbatim_quote: If a license is not renewed within five years, the licensee shall make an application for a license pursuant to Section 7066.
rules.notes: B&P 7143.5: a person not entitled to renew under 7141 may obtain a new license only by paying all fees and meeting all requirements for an original license.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 384-385 (B&P 7141(d); B&P 7143.5)
verification.note: Extra check (numeric process step): 5 years; new application under 7066; original-license fees and qualifications. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2014).

rules.title: Retroactive renewal if completed within 90 days of expiration
rules.plain_english: CSLB must grant a retroactive renewal (no break in licensure) if an otherwise eligible licensee submits a completed renewal application with the renewal fee and the delinquency fee within 90 days after the license expired. Delivery to CSLB headquarters or a postmark within the 90 days counts as submitted.

deemed_submitted_if: delivered to board headquarters within 90 days

rules.applies_to: Otherwise eligible licensees who missed the renewal deadline
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall grant the retroactive renewal of a license if, within 90 days of the expiration of the license, the otherwise eligible licensee submits a completed application for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar, and pays the appropriate renewal fee and delinquency fee prescribed by this chapter.
rules.notes: The application must be completed; an incomplete application does not qualify.

verification.note: 90 days, "shall grant", completed application, renewal plus delinquency fee, delivered-or-postmarked rule all match. SB 1474 effective 1/1/2021 confirmed.

rules.title: Suspended license must still be renewed but cannot be used
rules.plain_english: A suspended license still expires and must be renewed on schedule. Renewing it does not allow the contractor to do any licensed work while it remains suspended.
rules.verbatim_quote: A license that is suspended for any reason which constitutes a basis for suspension under this chapter, is subject to expiration and shall be renewed as provided in this chapter, but this renewal does not entitle the licensee, while the license remains suspended, and until it is reinstated, to engage in any activity to which the license relates

rules.title: Revoked license treated as expired; reinstatement needs original-license requirements
rules.plain_english: A revoked license counts as expired on the revocation date and cannot be renewed. To reinstate it, the licensee must apply, pay all fees and meet every requirement for an original license.

reinstatement_requirements: all qualifications and requirements for an original license

rules.verbatim_quote: A revoked license shall be considered as having expired as of the date of revocation and shall not be renewed. To reinstate a revoked license a licensee may apply for reinstatement of the license only if he pays all of the fees and meets all of the qualifications and requirements set forth in this chapter for obtaining an original license.

rules.title: Return rejected renewal within 90 days or it is abandoned
rules.plain_english: If CSLB rejects a renewal application as insufficient or incomplete, the contractor must return it within 90 days of the rejection date. Otherwise the application and fee are abandoned and cannot be reinstated, and a new application and fee are needed. A petition disputing the abandonment for good cause must be received within 90 days of the abandonment date.

parameters.consequence: application and fee deemed abandoned; not reinstatable; new application with fee required
parameters.petition_measured_from: date renewal application is deemed abandoned

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose renewal application was rejected
rules.verbatim_quote: If a licensee fails to return an application for renewal which was rejected for insufficiency or incompleteness within 90 days from the original date of rejection, the application and fee shall be deemed abandoned. Any application abandoned may not be reinstated.
rules.notes: The registrar may also refuse to renew a license because the licensee fails or refuses to complete the renewal application.

verification.note: 90 days from original rejection date; abandoned, not reinstatable; petition received within 90 days of abandonment on good cause, all match.

rules.title: Unpaid final tax/agency liabilities can block renewal or suspend license
rules.plain_english: CSLB may refuse to issue, reinstate, reactivate or renew a license, or may suspend it, if the licensee has unresolved final liabilities (taxes, penalties, interest or fees) owed to CSLB, DIR, EDD, the Franchise Tax Board or the State Board of Equalization.
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar may refuse to issue, reinstate, reactivate, or renew a license or may suspend a license for the failure of a licensee to resolve all outstanding final liabilities, which include taxes, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any fees that may be assessed by the board, the Department of Industrial Relations, the Employment Development Department ...
rules.notes: For FTB liabilities the section becomes operative within 60 days after CSLB gives FTB licensing information including FEIN/ITIN/SSN (7145.5(c)). License applications include an authorization for FTB to disclose tax information (7145.5(d)). The statute still names the State Board of Equalization; many former BOE tax programs are now administered by CDTFA, which this text does not mention.

verification.note: All five agencies, liability types and possible actions match. 60-day FTB operative rule in (c) matches the note. SB 800 effective 1/1/2018 confirmed.

rules.title: Personnel on a license suspended for unpaid liabilities barred; linked licenses suspended
rules.plain_english: While a license is suspended for unpaid liabilities, its qualifier and other personnel of record cannot serve in any licensed capacity; they may only work as non-supervising employees. Any other license that shares those personnel is also suspended until the debt is paid or the personnel disassociate.

restricted_persons: any other personnel of record named on the suspended license
parameters.linked_license_effect: other renewable licensed entity with same personnel of record is suspended
lifted_when: same personnel of record disassociate from the other entity

rules.applies_to: Qualifiers, officers and other personnel of record; affiliated licensed entities
rules.verbatim_quote: Until the debts covered by this section are satisfied, the qualifying person and any other personnel of record named on a license that has been suspended under this section shall be prohibited from serving in any capacity that is subject to licensure under this chapter, but shall be permitted to act in the capacity of a nonsupervising bona fide employee.
rules.notes: A compliance tool should check affiliated licenses (shared personnel of record) when one license is suspended under this section.

rules.title: CSLB must mail preliminary notice at least 60 days before liability refusal/suspension
rules.plain_english: CSLB can refuse or suspend a license for unpaid liabilities only after mailing a preliminary notice that names a date certain, at least 60 days before that date. The contractor has that window to resolve the debt.

parameters.notice_content: license will be refused or suspended by a date certain

rules.verbatim_quote: The refusal to issue a license or the suspension of a license as provided by this section shall be applicable only if the registrar has mailed a notice preliminary to the refusal or suspension that indicates that the license will be refused or suspended by a date certain. This preliminary notice shall be mailed to the licensee at least 60 days before the date certain.
rules.notes: A tool can compute days remaining from the notice to the date certain.

verification.note: Mailed preliminary notice at least 60 days before the date certain matches. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2018).

rules.title: BOE liability under an installment agreement does not trigger refusal/suspension
rules.plain_english: A State Board of Equalization liability does not cause refusal or suspension if the licensee has an installment payment agreement with the BOE for that liability and is complying with it.

parameters.exception_condition: installment payment agreement for that liability in effect and licensee in compliance with its terms

rules.applies_to: Licensees owing State Board of Equalization liabilities
rules.verbatim_quote: In the case of outstanding final liabilities assessed by the State Board of Equalization, this section shall not apply to any outstanding final liability if the licensee has entered into an installment payment agreement for that liability with the State Board of Equalization and is in compliance with the terms of that agreement.
rules.notes: The text grants this exception only for BOE liabilities. It does not state a similar exception for DIR, EDD or FTB debts.

rules.title: Home improvement article: 'person' = natural persons; senior citizen = age 65+
rules.plain_english: In the home improvement article, 'person' means only individuals (natural persons), and a 'senior citizen' is anyone 65 or older. Senior buyers get a five-day instead of three-day right to cancel.

parameters.person: natural persons only (overrides B&P 7025 definition for Article 10)

rules.verbatim_quote: (a) “Person” as used in this article is limited to natural persons, notwithstanding the definition of person in Section 7025. (b) “Senior citizen” means an individual who is 65 years of age or older.
rules.notes: Contract software should capture whether any buyer is 65+ to select the 5-day cancellation notice.

rules.title: Home improvement contractor (incl. pool contractors) must meet Article 10
rules.plain_english: Any licensed contractor, including a swimming pool contractor, who does home improvement work full time or part time is a home improvement contractor and must meet every requirement in Article 10.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors doing residential home improvement work
rules.verbatim_quote: A home improvement contractor, including a swimming pool contractor, is a contractor as defined and licensed under this chapter who is engaged in the business of home improvement either full time or part time. A home improvement contractor shall satisfy all requirements imposed by this article.

rules.title: What counts as 'home improvement' (incl. disaster rebuilds)
rules.plain_english: Home improvement means repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, modernizing or adding to residential property, plus rebuilding homes damaged in a declared natural disaster. It includes work like driveways, pools, spas, patios, solar, landscaping, fences, porches, garages and basements, and installing home improvement goods or services.

activities: reconstruction/restoration/rebuilding of residential property damaged or destroyed by a declared natural disaster
disaster_declaration_triggers: Governor state of emergency under Gov. Code 8625
Presidential emergency or major disaster declaration
examples: swimming pools, spas and hot tubs
other improvements of structures or land adjacent to a dwelling house

rules.applies_to: Classifying whether a residential job is home improvement (triggers B&P 7159 contract rules)
rules.verbatim_quote: “Home improvement” means the repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, or modernizing of, or adding to, residential property, as well as the reconstruction, restoration, or rebuilding of a residential property that is damaged or destroyed by a natural disaster for which a state of emergency is proclaimed by the Governor
rules.notes: New single-family home construction for an owner is covered separately by B&P 7164.

rules.title: Home improvement goods or services
rules.plain_english: Home improvement goods and services are goods and services bought in connection with improving real property, such as carpeting, texture coating, fencing, AC or heating equipment and termite extermination. Goods affixed so they become part of the property count even if removable.
rules.applies_to: Sellers and installers of residential goods and services
rules.verbatim_quote: Such home improvement goods and services include, but are not limited to, carpeting, texture coating, fencing, air conditioning or heating equipment, and termite extermination. Home improvement goods include goods which are to be so affixed to real property as to become a part of real property whether or not severable therefrom.

rules.title: Solar energy system: residential, 1 kW to 5 MW AC
rules.plain_english: For home improvement and solar disclosure rules, a solar energy system is a residential solar electric device producing at least 1 kW and no more than 5 MW AC peak that meets Public Resources Code 25782 eligibility criteria.

parameters.primary_purpose: collection and distribution of solar energy for generation of electricity

rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 388 and 431
rules.verbatim_quote: “solar energy system” means a solar energy device to be installed on a residential building or residential property that has the primary purpose of providing for the collection and distribution of solar energy for the generation of electricity, that produces at least one kilowatt, and not more than five megawatts, alternating current rated peak electricity
rules.notes: 7169(g) uses 'installed on a residential building' (text truncated at end of this chunk).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 388 and 431-432 (B&P 7151(c); B&P 7169(g))
verification.note: Extra check (numeric definition): 1 kW to 5 MW AC rated peak, PRC 25782. The rest of 7169(g) is on page 432 and is the same definition except that it omits "or residential property". Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2022).

rules.title: Home improvement contract: oral or written, owner or tenant
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contract is any agreement, oral or written or in several documents, between a contractor and an owner, or a contractor and a tenant (in any size building), for home improvement work, including all labor, services and materials. Agreements by any salesperson with an owner or tenant to sell, install or furnish home improvement goods or services also count.

counterparties: tenant (regardless of number of units in building)
parameters.also_covers: agreements by a salesperson (registered or not) with owner or tenant for sale/installation/furnishing of home improvement goods or services

rules.verbatim_quote: “Home improvement contract” means an agreement, whether oral or written, or contained in one or more documents, between a contractor and an owner or between a contractor and a tenant, regardless of the number of residence or dwelling units contained in the building in which the tenant resides
rules.notes: B&P 7159(b) adds the over-$500 aggregate price threshold for the B&P 7159 contract requirements.

rules.title: Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration required
rules.plain_english: Anyone who solicits, sells, negotiates or signs home improvement contracts (including pools, spas and hot tubs) on behalf of a licensed contractor must be registered with CSLB as a Home Improvement Salesperson.
rules.applies_to: Sales staff of home improvement contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A home improvement salesperson shall register with the board in order to engage in the business of, or act in the capacity of, a home improvement salesperson.
rules.effective: Section amended effective January 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 592, SB 861)
rules.notes: The book's history line shows a 2026 amendment but does not say which subdivision changed.

rules.title: HIS must disclose contractor's business name and license number first
rules.plain_english: Before soliciting or selling, a home improvement salesperson must tell the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they represent for that deal. An HIS may work for more than one contractor. Failing to disclose is grounds for discipline.

parameters.timing: before engaging in any soliciting, selling, negotiating or executing of contracts
parameters.violation: cause for disciplinary action under B&P 7155

rules.verbatim_quote: However, prior to engaging in any activity described in subdivision (a) of this section, a home improvement salesperson shall identify to the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they are representing for the purposes of that transaction. Failure to do so is a cause of disciplinary action within the meaning of Section 7155.

verification.note: Prior-to-activity disclosure of business name and license number; multiple employers allowed subject to 7154; discipline under 7155. SB 861 effective 1/1/2026 confirmed.

rules.title: Who does not need HIS registration
rules.plain_english: Officers of a licensed corporation, managers/members/officers of a licensed LLC, general partners, and the qualifier do not need HIS registration, but only if they are personnel of record on that license at the time of the sale. Retail-store salespeople (buyer-initiated, fixed location), appointment setters, and service repairpersons limited to the requested repair are also exempt.

exempt_persons: officer of record of a licensed corporation
manager, member or officer of record of a licensed LLC
general partner listed on the license record of a licensed partnership
salesperson whose sales come from buyer-initiated negotiations at a fixed-location general merchandise retail establishment
person contacting buyers only to schedule appointments for a registered HIS
bona fide service repairperson employed by a licensed contractor, limited to the service/repair/emergency repair initially requested
parameters.condition_for_first_four: listed as personnel of record for the licensee responsible for the transaction at the time of the sales transaction

rules.applies_to: Contractors deciding who must register as HIS
rules.verbatim_quote: The exemption to registration provided under paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subdivision (d) shall apply only to those individuals who, at the time of the sales transaction, are listed as personnel of record for the licensee responsible for soliciting, negotiating, or contracting for a service or improvement that is subject to regulation under this article.
rules.notes: Subdivision (e) names paragraphs (1)-(3); the qualifier is paragraph (3), so the personnel-of-record condition covers officers/LLC managers/members, general partners and qualifiers.

rules.title: Selling home improvement without HIS registration is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to work as a salesperson for a home improvement contractor, or to sell home improvement goods or services, without a current and valid HIS registration at the time of the sale. CSLB may also issue a citation.

parameters.offense: acting as home improvement salesperson without current valid registration at time of sales transaction

rules.verbatim_quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person to engage in the occupation of salesperson for one or more home improvement contractors within this state without having, at the time of the sales transaction, a current and valid home improvement salesperson registration issued by the registrar.
rules.notes: The contractor who employs an unregistered salesperson is also subject to discipline (B&P 7154(d)).

verification.note: Both misdemeanor paragraphs and the 7028.7 citation power (on probable cause) match. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2016).

rules.title: Security interest unenforceable if sale made by unregistered salesperson
rules.plain_english: If the home improvement contract was solicited by someone who was not a registered (or exempt) salesperson when the homeowner signed, any security interest the contractor took to secure payment cannot be enforced.

parameters.test_time: when the homeowner signs the home improvement contract

rules.applies_to: Contractors taking security interests on home improvement jobs
rules.verbatim_quote: Any security interest taken by a contractor, to secure any payment for the performance of any act or conduct described in Section 7151 ... is unenforceable if the person soliciting the act or contract was not a duly registered salesperson or was not exempt from registration pursuant to Section 7152 at the time the homeowner signs the home improvement contract solicited by the salesperson.

verification.note: Unenforceable security interest, acts on or after 1/1/1995, test at time homeowner signs, all match. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2016).

rules.title: HIS application: written form, fee and fingerprints
rules.plain_english: A salesperson applies for HIS registration in writing on CSLB's form with the required fee and must submit fingerprints (electronically where available) for DOJ and FBI criminal history checks. CSLB may deny registration on B&P 480 grounds.

required: full set of fingerprints (electronic where readily available)

rules.verbatim_quote: As part of an application for a home improvement salesperson, the board shall require an applicant to furnish a full set of fingerprints for purposes of conducting criminal history record checks.
rules.notes: Fee amount is not stated in this excerpt.

rules.title: HIS registration expires two years from last day of month issued
rules.plain_english: A Home Improvement Salesperson registration expires two years after the last day of the month it was issued, and after renewal, two years from the date it last expired.

parameters.anchor_original: last day of the month in which the registration was issued
parameters.anchor_renewed: date on which the renewed registration last expired

rules.applies_to: Registered home improvement salespersons and their employers
rules.verbatim_quote: All home improvement salesperson registrations issued under the provisions of this article shall expire two years from the last day of the month in which the registration was issued, or two years from the date on which the renewed registration last expired.
rules.notes: Employers should track each salesperson's expiration date; selling with an expired registration is a misdemeanor (B&P 7153).

verification.note: Two-year term from last day of month issued / date renewed registration last expired matches. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2016).

rules.title: Renew HIS registration before it expires
rules.plain_english: To renew an unexpired HIS registration, file the CSLB renewal form and pay the renewal fee before expiration; the renewal runs two more years.
rules.verbatim_quote: To renew a home improvement salesperson registration, which has not expired, the registrant shall before the time at which the registration would otherwise expire, apply for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and pay a renewal fee prescribed by this chapter.

rules.title: Late HIS renewal: within 3 years with 50% penalty
rules.plain_english: An HIS renewal is delinquent if not postmarked or electronically received by the expiration date. A registration can still be renewed within three years after expiration by paying the renewal fee plus a penalty equal to 50% of the renewal fee. After three years, a new application is required.

parameters.after_window: new application for registration under B&P 7153.1

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons with expired registrations
rules.verbatim_quote: A registration may, however, still be renewed at any time within three years after its expiration upon the filing of an application for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and the payment of the renewal fee prescribed by this chapter and a delinquent renewal penalty equal to 50 percent of the renewal fee.
rules.notes: Renewal fee amount is not in this excerpt.

verification.note: Delinquent if not postmarked or electronically received by expiration; 3-year window; 50% of renewal fee; new application after 3 years. Operative 7/1/2017 confirmed.

rules.title: Rejected HIS renewal: 90 days to return; 90-day petition window
rules.plain_english: If an HIS renewal is rejected as incomplete, the registrant must return it within 90 days of rejection or it is abandoned (a new application is then required). A good-cause petition disputing abandonment must be received within 90 days of the abandonment date.

parameters.consequence: application and fee deemed abandoned; new application under B&P 7153.1

rules.verbatim_quote: If a registrant fails to return the application rejected for insufficiency or incompleteness within 90 days from the original date of rejection, the application and fee shall be deemed abandoned.

verification.note: 90 days from original rejection; new application under 7153.1; petition within 90 days of abandonment. Quote also appears in 7145 (page 385) in near-identical form; checked against 7153.3(c).

rules.title: Notify CSLB before a registered salesperson starts work
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor must file CSLB's form reporting the employment of a registered salesperson, including the salesperson's name and registration number, before the salesperson begins working for the contractor.

parameters.deadline: before the home improvement salesperson begins work for the contractor
parameters.electronic_filing: allowed if board implements system under B&P 7156.6

rules.verbatim_quote: A home improvement contractor licensed under this chapter shall notify the registrar in writing, on a form prescribed by the registrar, about the employment of a registered home improvement salesperson ... The form shall be submitted prior to the home improvement salesperson beginning work for the contractor.
rules.notes: Until CSLB has received this notice, the salesperson may not guide an owner in selecting a contractor (B&P 7156(c)).

verification.note: Registrar form, name and registration number, submitted before the salesperson begins work. SB 561 effective 1/1/2016 confirmed.

rules.title: Notify CSLB within 90 days after a salesperson leaves
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor must notify CSLB on its form, with the salesperson's name and registration number, within 90 days after a registered salesperson stops working for the contractor.

parameters.measured_from: date the salesperson ceases to be employed

rules.verbatim_quote: The form shall be submitted within 90 days after the home improvement salesperson ceases to be employed by the contractor.

verification.note: Within 90 days after the salesperson ceases employment matches.

rules.title: Contractor discipline for not reporting salespersons or using unregistered ones
rules.plain_english: A contractor who fails to file the salesperson hire or termination notices, or who uses an unregistered person to sell home improvement contracts, is subject to CSLB discipline.

violations: employing unregistered person to sell home improvement contracts

rules.verbatim_quote: A home improvement contractor who employs a person to sell home improvement contracts while that person is not registered by the registrar as a home improvement salesperson as provided in this article, is subject to disciplinary action by the registrar.

verification.note: Both discipline grounds match. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2016).

rules.title: HIS registration may be suspended or revoked for violations
rules.plain_english: Any violation of the contractors law by a home improvement salesperson is cause for discipline; CSLB may suspend or revoke the registration through Administrative Procedure Act proceedings.
rules.verbatim_quote: Violation of any provision of this chapter by a home improvement salesperson constitutes cause for disciplinary action. The registrar may suspend or revoke the registration of the home improvement salesperson if he or she is found to be in violation.

verification.note: Suspend or revoke; Gov. Code 11500 et seq. procedure matches. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2012).

rules.title: Contractor disciplined for its salesperson's violations, even without knowledge
rules.plain_english: If a home improvement salesperson violates the law, the contractor who employed them at the time can be disciplined too, whether or not the contractor knew about or took part in the violation.

parameters.liable_party: contractor employing the salesperson at the time of the violation

rules.verbatim_quote: Violations of any provisions of this chapter by a home improvement salesperson likewise constitute cause for disciplinary action against the contractor, by whom he or she was employed at the time the violation occurred, whether or not the contractor had knowledge of or participated in the act or omission constituting violations of this chapter.

verification.note: Employer at time of violation; knowledge or participation not required. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (Amended effective January 1, 2016).

rules.title: Salesperson must account for and remit all payments to employing contractor
rules.plain_english: A home improvement salesperson who fails to account for or turn over to the employing contractor any payment received on a job commits a misdemeanor and is subject to discipline.

parameters.duty: account for and remit every payment received to the employing contractor
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.title: No paying owners for referrals or placing business with others

rules.title: Mechanics Lien Warning (home improvement contract version)
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include the statutory 'Mechanics Lien Warning' explaining liens, 20-day preliminary notices, how to protect against liens with a subcontractor/supplier list and joint checks, and CSLB contact information.

parameters.required_text:
MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a ‘Preliminary Notice.’ This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if they are not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB’s internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752).
REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 (except bonded contractors under 7159.5(a)(8))
rules.verbatim_quote: BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
rules.notes: In the book the phone number line is printed as '800-321-CSLB (2752) .REMEMBER' (typesetting); the period placement here is normalized. The B&P 7164 single-family-dwelling version has slightly different wording.

Contact CSLB for information about the licensed contractor you are considering, including information about disclosable complaints, disciplinary actions, and civil judgments that are reported to CSLB.

Your only remedy may be in civil court, and you may be liable for damages arising out of any injuries to the unlicensed contractor or the unlicensed contractor’s employees.
For more information:

Call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)
Write CSLB at P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.

parameters.required_text:
YOUR RIGHTS TO CANCEL BEFORE WORK BEGINS
(A) You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract until:
1. You receive a copy of this contract signed and dated by you and the contractor; and
2. The contractor starts work.
(B) However, even if the work has begun you, the buyer, may still cancel the contract for any of the reasons specified in items 1 through 4 of this paragraph. If any of these reasons occur, you may cancel the contract within three business days of signing the contract for normal service and repairs, or within seven business days of signing a contract to repair or correct conditions resulting from any sudden or catastrophic event for which a state of emergency has been declared by the President of the United States or the Governor, or for which a local emergency has been declared by the executive officer or governing body of any city, county, or city and county:
1. You may cancel the contract if the price, including all labor and materials, is more than seven hundred fifty dollars ($750).
2. You may cancel the contract if you did not initiate the contact with the contractor to request the work.
3. You may cancel the contract if the contractor sold you goods or services beyond those reasonably necessary to take care of the particular problem that caused you to contact the contractor.
4. You may cancel the contract if the payment was due or the contractor accepted any money before the work was complete.
(C) If any of these reasons for canceling occurred, you may cancel the contract as specified under paragraph (B) above by e-mailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business within three business days or, if applicable, seven business days of the date you received a signed and dated copy of this contract. Include your name, your address, and the date you received a signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received it, any goods delivered to you under this contract. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.

rules.title: Mechanics Lien Warning (single-family dwelling contract version)

parameters.required_text:
MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a ‘Preliminary Notice.’ This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if he or she is not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB’s Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752).
REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe.
